cover.title: Progress 2026
cover.subtitle: A year of findings for Corvache — and a brief for what we'd propose next.

sender.name: Mara Lindqvist
sender.note: Hi team — sharing our summary of findings from the year plus a brief for what we'd propose next. Nothing here is final; I'd love your read before we lock the direction.

sections.heading: A strong year of quiet compounding
body: 2025 was less about a single breakout moment and more about steady, compounding gains across every channel we touch. Demand grew fastest at the top — configurator sessions more than doubled — but the more durable story is the order book: the deposit holders we earned in Q1 are still with us in Q4, and they're speccing richer builds each time they come back.

The repositioning we ran in spring — away from spec-sheet messaging and toward the silence story, restraint as the brand's real performance claim — is the clearest driver we can point to. It shows up in the numbers below and, just as tellingly, in social listening: people have started describing the car in Corvache's own words.

stats.label: Lift in average option spend per build

items.title: The engineering story outperformed the spec sheet 3 to 1
items.body: Films built around the silence lab and the marque's motorsport lineage consistently out-engaged range-and-torque posts, especially with first-time EV considerers — the audience most skeptical of claims and most moved by craft.

items.title: The order book, not the funnel, is now the bigger lever
items.body: Cost per configurator session held roughly flat year over year, but the deposit holders we already have are returning more often — and every return visit specs a richer build.

items.title: Owner-shot photography earned the highest save rate
items.body: Road photography from early owners and drive-experience guests outperformed studio renders on saves and shares by a wide margin, suggesting an underused content well.

items.title: Email remains undervalued relative to its return
items.body: Email drove a disproportionate share of configurator returns and option upgrades relative to the media budget allocated to it — the smallest line item with the clearest ROI.

sections.heading: A brief for the next project
body: We'd propose leaning further into the engineering story with a dedicated film-and-photography series for early 2026 — working title "Grand Tours" — built around the owner imagery that's already outperforming our studio work. Real owners, long roads, no soundtrack: the silence positioning, demonstrated rather than claimed.

In parallel, we'd like to rebuild the email program around the order-book data above: fewer, better-timed sends, segmented by where someone sits between first configuration and delivery rather than blasted to the full list.
If this direction feels right, our next step would be a short creative sprint to storyboard the first three Grand Tours pieces for your review.

sections.heading: What we'd lock before the sprint
sections.intro: Nothing below is contractual — it's the working scope behind the brief above, as we understand it today. Confirm or challenge any row before we kick off.

rows.assumption: 2026 brand program: the Grand Tours series, the email program rebuild, and the retained media strategy — one integrated engagement rather than three separate statements of work
Three Grand Tours pieces storyboarded in the sprint; a full-season greenlight follows your review of the first three
Submission flow with usage rights baked into the upload; nothing runs uncleared, and legal reviews the consent language before the flow ships
US, UK, Germany and Switzerland at launch — the four markets carrying 82% of the current order book — with the Nordics as a fast-follow once delivery capacity opens
Deposit holders and configurator returners first; conquest audiences only after the retention program ships
Fewer, better-timed sends segmented by where someone sits between first configuration and delivery; full-list blasts retired entirely
Brand-media return reported as a modeled 3–5× range with the method footnoted; the 61% retention and 2.4× configurator figures stay measured and untouched
Brand flights hold at 2025 levels; reallocated budget goes to email and CRM rather than new paid channels this cycle
$940K program total — production, media, email platform work, and honoraria for owner shoots — pending finance review of the Q1 phasing
Sprint W1–2, storyboards W3, client review W4; first Grand Tours piece in market by April
Retail and showroom experience, motor-show presence, dealer co-op media, and product launch reveals — all handled by other partners this cycle
Owner-photo rights clearance lead times, EV incentive changes shifting Q4 demand reads, and platform API changes limiting social-listening continuity

cta.heading: What do you think?
cta.body: This is meant to be a conversation, not a verdict. Comment on any section above, or download the full write-up to share with the rest of your team.

exec-summary.name: Devon Reyes
exec-summary.text: Love this framing — the order-book story is exactly what we should be leading with. This is the narrative I've been trying to articulate internally for months.

replies.name: Priya Anand
replies.text: Agreed it's the right story. One flag on the word 'compounding' though — it implies the gains are building on each other, but a lot of this could just be the spring repositioning finally landing. Are we sure it's compounding and not a one-time step change?

replies.name: Mara Lindqvist
replies.text: Fair distinction. We read it as compounding because the Q1 deposit cohort keeps re-engaging quarter over quarter — that's the same audience getting more valuable over time, not a single lift. But I'll tighten the language so it's a claim we can defend rather than a vibe.

replies.name: Devon Reyes
replies.text: 'The same audience getting more valuable over time' — honestly just use that sentence. It's clearer than 'compounding.'

replies.name: Mara Lindqvist
replies.text: Ha — stealing it. Done.

data-points.name: Priya Anand
data-points.text: Before this goes anywhere near the board deck, I want to flag the 4.1× return on brand media spend. It's tagged 'Modeled,' but sitting next to two 'Measured' numbers, everyone in that room is going to read all four as hard fact.

replies.name: Devon Reyes
replies.text: I hear you, but this is the strongest story we've had since the reveal. If we water it down with caveats nobody's going to feel it — the board responds to conviction, not asterisks.

replies.name: Priya Anand
replies.text: Conviction is great right up until finance asks how we got to 4.1 and we don't have a clean answer. I'm not saying bury it — I'm saying don't dress a model up as a measurement.

replies.name: Nick Zinner
replies.text: @Priya Anand fair challenge. The 4.1× comes out of a media-mix model against the brand-campaign flights — it's directional, not attributable to the dollar. I'd stand behind the direction (roughly 3–5×), less so the decimal. Happy to share the model doc.

replies.name: Priya Anand
replies.text: That's exactly my point though. If the honest version is '3–5×, modeled,' let's present it as a range. A range reads as rigor; a single decimal reads as false precision.

replies.name: Jessie Harte
replies.text: For what it's worth, our board actually likes ranges — they've been burned by point estimates before. I'd rather walk in with '3–5× (modeled)' that survives the follow-up question than 4.1× that doesn't.

replies.name: Devon Reyes
replies.text: Okay — I can live with a range if we frame it as upside. I still don't want the retention number touched, though. 61% is measured and it's the best line in the deck.

replies.name: Mara Lindqvist
replies.text: This is a good disagreement to have now instead of in the room. Proposal: keep 61% and 2.4× exactly as-is (both measured), present the brand-media return as '3–5×, modeled,' and footnote the method. @Nick Zinner can you swap the tile to a range and attach the model doc? If that works for everyone, I'll call it settled.

replies.name: Priya Anand
replies.text: Works for me. Thanks for hearing it out rather than defending the decimal.

replies.name: Devon Reyes
replies.text: Agreed. Good call on the footnote — best of both.

engagement-trend.name: Jessie Harte
engagement-trend.text: Is the Q4 jump partly seasonal? We always get a year-end bump — the show calendar plus December delivery timing — and I don't want to over-read a spike that comes back every winter.

replies.name: Nick Zinner
replies.text: Good instinct. It's partly seasonal, but Q4 2025 is up ~28% over Q4 2024 on the same seasonal baseline, so there's real underlying growth on top of the year-end effect. I can add the year-over-year overlay if that's useful.

replies.name: Jessie Harte
replies.text: Yes please — the YoY overlay is exactly what'll keep me honest when I present it.

key-findings.name: Devon Reyes
key-findings.text: Finding #4 is the one that stings — we've been underfunding email for years and it's quietly outperforming everything. Can we make this louder?

replies.name: Priya Anand
replies.text: Strong agree. Email is the least glamorous line item and the highest ROI. If we're reallocating budget for 2026, this is where I'd start.

replies.name: Mara Lindqvist
replies.text: Noted — we'll pull email forward in the recommendation and put a real number against it instead of leaving it as a footnote.

recommendation.name: Devon Reyes
recommendation.text: 'Grand Tours' is a great name. Green-light the creative sprint from our side — I want to see the first three storyboards.

replies.name: Priya Anand
replies.text: Before we build a whole series on owner photography — do we have the rights locked? We've had two near-misses this year using owner photos without clean usage terms, and I don't want that to become a Q1 fire drill.

replies.name: Ray Okafor
replies.text: @Priya Anand that's on my radar. The plan is a submission flow with explicit usage rights baked into the upload — nothing runs that isn't cleared. I'll add a rights slide to the sprint brief so it's built in, not bolted on.

replies.name: Jessie Harte
replies.text: Appreciate that, Ray. Legal will want to see the consent language before anything ships, but if it's there from the start we're in good shape.

replies.name: Mara Lindqvist
replies.text: Perfect — so we're go on the sprint, rights handled up front, first three storyboards back to you for review. @Devon Reyes I'll send the schedule today. Thanks all — this is exactly the read we were hoping for.
